video_metadata.title: The VWAP Fade I Trade Every Day on Micro Nasdaq | Quant Walkthrough

input.transcript_snippet: OK so today I want to walk through the exact VWAP fade setup I trade on Micro Nasdaq, MNQ. Five-minute bars, regular trading hours only — I do not touch this overnight. The setup is simple. I'm waiting for price to get one and a half standard deviations above session VWAP. Then I want it to hold there for at least two bars. Once it holds and starts to roll back inside, that's my entry — short. I size based on ATR, my stop is one and a half times ATR — usually that puts me about twelve points away on MNQ. My target is back to VWAP or one and a half ATR adverse, whichever hits first. The big rule: ADX has to be below twenty-two. If we're trending, this trade does not work — period. I learned that the hard way last year, blew through three Topstep accounts trying to fade trends. Disable this strategy on FOMC days, CPI mornings, NFP. The numbers I run on a fifty K simulated account: profit factor about one point nine, Sharpe one point six, sixty percent win rate. Average daily P&L around three hundred bucks. So that's the strategy.

strategies.description: Fade extensions of MNQ price 1.5 std-dev above/below session VWAP after 2-bar hold; ADX < 22 regime gate; RTH only; disable on FOMC/CPI/NFP per Algorithmic Edge YouTube walkthrough.
strategies.entry_condition: Enter short when price extends 1.5 sigma above VWAP for 2 bars then rolls back inside; mirror long. Skip FOMC/CPI/NFP days. Require ADX < 22.
